label: Identity
description: An epistery digital identity — an IdentityContract on chain. It is a collection of interchangeable device keys (rivets), any one of which can act for it, and a set of sections: one per session the identity runs, each carrying that session's on-chain access list. A section's reserved `default` entry is the role every address holds on it, so whether a session is open to the world is a chain fact, not a setting on a server. Epistery-published vocabulary; the contract state is re-readable by anyone and scan's copy is a cache of it. What each session IS — its kind, name and title — is declared by the host the identity is named under, and linked rather than restated.

identity.note: The contract address is the identity. A name is a label one host resolves to it, and different hosts may name the same contract differently.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The IdentityContract address — the identity itself.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The world-readable display name the contract publishes in its `_profile` section.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The host this identity is named under — the one that resolves its name and serves its page.

fields.name: profileUrl
fields.description: The identity's own page on that host.

fields.name: home
fields.description: The host's open contract-home read. Fetched with a caller's own identity it answers with the sessions THAT caller may open.

fields.name: model
fields.description: Which generation of the contract this is: `access` (rivets + sections, current), `chat-v3` (the messaging generation), `legacy` (owner + rivets).

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The device that deployed the contract. Provenance only — it holds no power the other rivets lack.

fields.name: host
fields.description: The rivet designated as the default recovery signer. A rivet like any other, revocable; absent when the identity keeps no recovery key.

fields.name: rivets
fields.description: The devices that can act as this identity. Each device carries its owner-given name, when it was added, and whether it publishes an encryption key others can wrap to.

fields.name: sessions
fields.description: The identity's sessions. Each carries the on-chain access facts (the world's default role, the count of named collaborators) and, where the host declares it, what the session is and where to open it.

fields.name: openSessionCount
fields.description: How many of those sessions grant a role to every address — the ones a walk-up visitor can open.

fields.name: sessionCount
fields.description: Every session section on the contract, open or not.

fields.name: removeRivetThreshold
fields.description: How many rivets must agree to remove one — the identity's own governance knob.

fields.name: messageCount
fields.description: Messages the contract has received directly on chain.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: The chain the contract lives on.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The block explorer's page for the contract — where anyone re-reads every figure here.

trust.note: Reserved — identity trust factors (device count and age, continuity of the creator device, the two-sided binding between the name a host serves and the contract on chain) declared here as the market defines them. The contract itself is the primary fact.
